animations.name: accordion-down
animations.css: @keyframes accordion-down { from { height: 0 } to { height: var(--radix-accordion-content-height) } }
animations.description: Expands accordion content from collapsed to full height

animations.name: accordion-up
animations.css: @keyframes accordion-up { from { height: var(--radix-accordion-content-height) } to { height: 0 } }
animations.description: Collapses accordion content from full height to zero

animations.name: spin
animations.css: @keyframes spin { from { transform: rotate(0deg) } to { transform: rotate(360deg) } }
animations.description: Continuous rotation animation for loading spinners

animations.name: hero-search-band
animations.description: Custom animation applied to hero search band element, likely JS-driven based on class name pattern

animations.name: global-ease
animations.css: transition: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, opacity, box-shadow, transform, translate, scale, rotate, filter, backdrop-filter 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
animations.description: Default global transition applied to interactive elements with ease-in-out timing

animations.name: opacity-fade
animations.description: Opacity transition for fade effects on overlays and mobile navigation

animations.name: logo-marquee
animations.description: JS-driven horizontal scrolling animation for partner logo strip, uses will-change: transform for GPU acceleration

insights: The design system employs a strict monochromatic palette (black/white) with inverted color schemes for dark and light sections, allowing full-bleed section transitions without visible dividers.
All primary buttons use rounded-full (pill) shapes with consistent height sizing (h-8 for small, h-10/h-12 for large CTAs), creating a cohesive action vocabulary across the entire page.
The navigation uses mix-blend-difference mode for the logo and text to automatically adapt colors based on underlying content, eliminating the need for multiple nav color variants.
